items.informal_name: Pullback of a dependent function with finite support along an injective function
items.type:
{ι : Type u} →
  {β : ι → Type v} →
    {κ : Type u_1} →
      [inst : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)] → (h : κ → ι) → Function.Injective h → (Π₀ (i : ι), β i) → Π₀ (k : κ), β (h k)
items.informal_description: Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be types, and let $\beta$ be a family of types indexed by $\iota$, where each type $\beta(i)$ has a zero element. Given an injective function $h : \kappa \to \iota$ and a dependent function with finite support $f : \Pi_0(i:\iota), \beta(i)$, `DFinsupp.comapDomain` constructs a new dependent function with finite support over the domain $\kappa$. This new function is defined as the pre-composition $f \circ h$, which maps an element $k \in \kappa$ to $f(h(k)) \in \beta(h(k))$. The injectivity of $h$ is required to ensure that the resulting function also has finite support.

items.informal_name: ComapDomain Application Equality for Dependent Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {β : ι → Type v} {κ : Type u_1} [inst : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)] (h : κ → ι) (hh : Function.Injective h)
  (f : Π₀ (i : ι), β i) (k : κ), (DFinsupp.comapDomain h hh f) k = f (h k)
items.informal_description: Let $ h : \kappa \to \iota $ be an injective function, and let $ f $ be a dependent finite support function from $ \iota $ to a family of types $ \beta(i) $ (each equipped with a zero element). For any $ k \in \kappa $, the value of the function obtained by reindexing $ f $ via $ h $ at $ k $ is equal to $ f(h(k)) $. In symbols, $ (\text{comapDomain}(h, f))(k) = f(h(k)) $.

items.informal_name: ComapDomain Preserves Single Elements Under Injective Functions
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {β : ι → Type v} {κ : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq κ]
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)] (h : κ → ι) (hh : Function.Injective h) (k : κ) (x : β (h k)),
  DFinsupp.comapDomain h hh (DFinsupp.single (h k) x) = DFinsupp.single k x
items.informal_description: Given an injective function $ h : \kappa \to \iota $ and an element $ x $ in $ \beta(h(k)) $, applying the comapDomain operation to the single non-zero function at index $ h(k) $ yields the single non-zero function at index $ k $. Formally, $ \text{comapDomain}_h(\text{single}_{h(k)}(x)) = \text{single}_k(x) $, where all types have decidable equality and each $ \beta(i) $ contains a zero element.

items.informal_name: Contravariant Map for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  {β : Type u_2} →
    {M : Type u_5} → [inst : Zero M] → (f : α → β) → (l : β →₀ M) → Set.InjOn f (f ⁻¹' ↑l.support) → α →₀ M
items.informal_description: Given a function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $, a finite support function $ l : \beta \to_0 M $, and a proof that $ f $ is injective on the preimage of $ \text{support}(l) $, this constructs a finite support function $ \alpha \to_0 M $ whose support is the preimage of $ \text{support}(l) $ under $ f $, and which maps each $ a \in \alpha $ to $ l(f(a)) $. The injectivity condition ensures the preimage remains finite.

items.informal_name: ComapDomain of a Single Function Under Injectivity
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [inst : Zero M] (f : α → β) (a : α) (m : M)
  (hif : Set.InjOn f (f ⁻¹' ↑(Finsupp.single (f a) m).support)),
  Finsupp.comapDomain f (Finsupp.single (f a) m) hif = Finsupp.single a m
items.informal_description: Given a function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $, an element $ a \in \alpha $, and a value $ m \in M $, if $ f $ is injective on the preimage of the support of the finite support function $ \text{single}(f a, m) $, then the contravariant map $ \text{comapDomain} \, f $ applied to $ \text{single}(f a, m) $ yields the finite support function $ \text{single}(a, m) $.
